evals.prompt: You are the Task Executor. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/task-executor.md`. Your task file content is in `.planning/evals/fixtures/sample-task.json`. The manifest is at `.planning/evals/fixtures/sample-manifest.json`. This is iteration 1. The task specifies POST /api/bookmarks returns 201. However, you discover during implementation that the Drizzle ORM returns snake_case field names (folder_id instead of folderId). Implement the task, noting any drift accurately.
evals.expected_output: The executor should complete the task but report structural drift — the assumption A01 specifies camelCase 'folderId' but the ORM returns 'folder_id'. The completion record should accurately describe this as structural drift with the broken assumption identified.
expectations: The completion record has matched_plan set to false
The drift_type is 'structural' (not 'local' — the API response shape is an external surface other tasks depend on)
The broken_assumptions array references assumption A01 by id
The broken_assumptions entry describes the reality (snake_case field names from Drizzle ORM)
The executor does NOT stop or fail because of the drift — it completes the task and records the deviation

evals.expected_output: The executor should NOT rewrite existing test files. It should check what's on disk, determine implementation is incomplete, and continue from where iteration 1 stopped.
expectations: The executor does NOT rewrite test files that already exist
The executor checks what files are already on disk before writing anything
The executor continues implementation from where it left off — creating the missing React components
